text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **
English monarch JOHN, who was forced by his rebellious barons to sign the Magna Carta at Runnymede, was born in 1167.
Spanish founder of the Jesuit order IGNATIUS LOYOLA was born in 1491.
American frontiersman KIT CARSON, who was an Indian agent, was born in 1809.

Australian artist PORTIA GEACH, who founded the New South Wales Housewives Association, was born in 1873. She was expelled from the association after accusing it of being a front for the Meadow-Lea Margarine Company in 1941.
The Australian pioneer of kindergarten and sex education ZOE BENJAMIN was born in 1882.

American billionaire HOWARD HUGHES was born in 1905. The US aviator, aircraft designer, film producer and entrepreneur founded the Hughes Aircraft Company and broke the air speed record in his own designed craft in 1935. He reached a speed of 566 kilometres an hour. In the 1920s he formed the Hughes film studio and produced "Hell's Angels" (1930), "Scarface" (1932) and "The Outlaw"(1944). He also invested in Las Vegas real estate and airlines but lived like a hermit. He developed a mania about germs and feared human contact. He died in 1976.

American actress AVA GARDNER, who appeared in "The Barefoot Contessa" and "Night of the Iguana", was born in 1922. While in Melbourne making the movie "On The Beach" she was asked what the film was about and reportedly replied "The End of the world...and Melbourne is the perfect location".
Irish folk musician EDDIE FURY was born in 1944. He and his brother formed the "FURYS".
British synthesizer player with 'Human League' IAN BURDEN was born in 1957.
** EVENTS **
1508 : London houses received piped water for the first
time.
1524 : Portuguese navigator VASCO DA GAMA died.
1828 : WILLIAM BURKE went on trial, charged with robbing
graves to sell corpses for medical research.
1914 : The first German bomb landed on British soil.
1925 : Italian leader MUSSOLINI declared himself
answerable only to the King of Italy.
1942 : Australian prime minister MR CURTIN cabled US

President ROOSEVELT thanking America for helping Australia in the Solomons. ROOSEVELT replied "I am very grateful to you for your congratulations...I am delighted that our joint forces are doing so splendidly in New Guinea".
1951 : Libya was declared indep*ndent.
1969 : More than four months after the brutal slaying of

seven people in Los Angeles members of the "Manson family" were charged with murder. Actress Sharon Tate, supermarket tycoon LENO LABIANCA and five others were murdered in the killing frenzy. Leader of the commune CHARLES MANSON, and three teenage girls and a male member of the "family" were charged with the murders. MANSON, a 35-year-old veteran criminal, preyed on young drifters, wooing then from the streets and taking them to a hideout in the desert. Investigators uncovered tales of bizarre goings-on with MANSON calling himself "JESUS CHRIST" and increasing his following through his own charisma and the use of LSD and other drugs.
1974 : The 'Beatles' partnership was legally dissolved.
1974 : Former British Labour minister JOHN STONEHOUSE,

who was thought drowned off Miami, Florida, surfaced in Melbourne. Police apprehended STONEHOUSE on the belief he was the Earl of Lucan, who was wanted for the murder of his children's nanny. STONEHOUSE was wanted in Britain over missing company funds and claimed life insurance policies.
1989 : Deposed Panamanian leader MANUEL NORIEGA gave
himself up to the papal nuncio in Panama City, having evaded American troops.

(Compiled from ABC ARCHIVES, ABC RADIO NATIONAL, "On This Day" published by REED INTERNATIONAL BOOKS LIMITED, "The Chronicle Of The 20th Century" published by PENGUIN BOOKS and "Rock And Pop (Day By Day)" published by BLANDFORD BOOKS.)
